rubric_notes: All five families with correct sunids and TAF-family membership verified against children listings; fold a.22 single-superfamily fact verified. Distinguishes family-level versus superfamily-level relatedness, explains the basis of the superfamily homology claim, and states that placement does not transfer function, DNA-binding mode, partner specificity or nucleosome-forming ability. Correctly notes fold-only similarity would not establish homology. Name matches (H1 a.4.5.13, HDAC, Dot1l, SET7/9, p300) supported by its search evidence; 'not evolutionarily related' slightly overstates SCOPe's non-assertion. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct sccs, sunids, names, species, 7-93 boundary. Correct interpretation: superfamily implies probable common ancestry, separate families mean no close sequence relationship, fold alone would not establish homology; rejects PRA-PH/MazG activity transfer, pathway, active site, oligomer state, orthology; Li/UNL not functional evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct superfamily c.55.1 (sunid 53067) and families c.55.1.1/53068, c.55.1.3/53083, c.55.1.4/53089, all supported by the children listing in the bundle; lineage c > c.55 > c.55.1 supported. Superfamily correctly interpreted as probable common ancestry with conserved two-lobed ATP-binding core; explicitly rejects transfer of substrate, reaction, cellular role, regulation, oligomeric behaviour, catalytic residues and template use; states homology is not proven by fold similarity alone. All must_include met, no must_avoid violated. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Family/superfamily/fold identifiers correct and bundle-supported. Interprets shared superfamily as homology with diverged chemistry, rejects transfer of mechanism/metal/substrate/oligomeric state without family-level, sequence-level and experimental evidence, warns that structure or AlphaFold hits show fold not activity, and distinguishes fold from superfamily. Lists a 'bacterioferritin-type' family within a.25.1 that does not exist as a family (bacterioferritin is a protein under a.25.1.1); minor hierarchy slip. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

All three families and sunids correct under b.6.1; sibling families and the superfamily comment 'contains copper-binding site' are supported by the children/annotations bundle and correctly interpreted as not a per-family guarantee. Superfamily = probable common origin; function transfer rejected with required evidence (conserved ligand residues, bound metal, assays). Example identifiers d5n0ya1 / Ephrin-B2 are not in its bundle but are correct public SCOPe entries. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct hierarchy with sunids, supported by sccs tree calls. Good superfamily-homology/function-divergence reasoning; rejects conjugation, UBX->Ras, RBD->p97, interface transfer, and fold-only homology. Minor issue: claims that name searches 'returned nothing', a process claim with no supporting search response in the bundle; noncentral.

Correct supported hierarchy and sunids (52172, 52171, 51349, 52173, 52252, 82344, d1r8ja2 2-135); homology_implied_by_level=true, no warnings, and the swapped-dimer linker annotation are all in the bundle. Reasoning: superfamily-level common ancestry, families not close relatives, fold alone is purely structural; rejects phosphorelay receiver function, Asp/Mg2+ phosphotransfer, catalysis in the wing, and residue-level/ligand/partner transfer; notes KaiA clock role is not shown by classification. Noncentral factual error: says the wing packs against a 'catalytic PLP-binding TIM-barrel domain', but the ODC in c.23.1.4 (Lactobacillus) has a c.67.1.5 fold-type I major domain, not a TIM barrel. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Identifiers, five-superfamily list, family and two protein nodes all supported by bundle (including the family children endpoint). Correctly separates fold-level topology claim from superfamily-level homology claim, says homology covers only b.84.5 members and not the hybrid-motif superfamilies, notes convergence possible, and addresses family-vs-superfamily closeness. Speculation that it was 'probably added in a later release' is hedged and not asserted as fact. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct fold and superfamily identifiers with sunids and release 2.08, all supported by the bundle. States superfamily is the ancestry level, fold is architecture only, and that the shared bundle may reflect convergence or undetectable distant ancestry. Requires new sequence, structural or functional evidence before merging; rejects function/heme-ligation/template transfer and correctly limits what a FATCAT/DALI hit can show. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct identifiers and sibling families supported by bundle. Superfamily = probable common ancestry of the nucleotide-binding domain; separate families = remote; functions diverged (cofactor-binding half of MDR with separate catalytic domain, CoA-binding, regulatory RCK) and explicit refusal to transfer function, substrate, mechanism, catalytic residues or ligand identity. Fold vs superfamily distinction correct. Minor: a hypothetical about 'other superfamilies in fold c.2' presupposes siblings that do not exist in 2.08, but it is framed conditionally. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Lineage and identifiers correct. States 'in SCOPe a shared superfamily implies homology' and answers 'Yes', then qualifies via the designed-proteins class; mentions the question's 'not true family-specific pair' framing but never retrieves or cites the actual family-node comment 'not a true family'. Also asserts a 'shared design lineage' without evidence. Transfer limits are appropriate. Decisive annotation ignored: bio 2; factual 2.

2.08 state correct and verified (shared c.23.14; c.23.14.2 vs c.23.14.1; current SIDs d1t1ja1/d1t1jb1), interpretation as distant superfamily-level homology with no function transfer. 1.69 side is recollection only ('classified separately, no recognised relationship') and omits the c.137.1.1 own-fold placement; honestly states 1.69 was not retrieved. No must_avoid violations.

Correct tag identification (class l, Tags lineage, N-terminal Tags, Synthetic, l.1.1.1, sunid 343393, H:1-8) and correct d1a14h1 9-111 b.1.1.1 VH with Fab NC10 comment, all supported. Homology warning and homology_implied_by_level=false cited. 'Homology implied at superfamily level' for d1a14h1 is a loose paraphrase of SCOP semantics, not a material error. Rejects tag matches as ancestry evidence, recommends masking, reports sequence 404 honestly.

Correct 1.75 f.11.1.1 and 2.08 two-class split with strong modules interpretation and per-domain search guidance. Omits the 2.04 split pinpoint. The 3tewA 96.9 percent and PA14-in-glycosidases points go beyond its thin (2.08 parents only) bundle but are correctly framed and not decisive.

Correct identifiers, boundaries and lineages; new fold d.394 and mosaic reading with reuse-vs-innovation distinction and function-transfer limits. Caveat describing the bromodomain as 'a fold-recognition placement' misstates the hierarchy: SCOPe places d3jb9a4 in the Bromodomain family a.29.2.1, a family-level homology assertion. Some literature claims (degenerate endonuclease) presented without SCOPe support but flagged as outside the hierarchy. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Concise and complete: family lineage, 're' flag on two domains, 'single repeat', canonical repeat representative with coordinate-scope caveat. Correctly ties family membership to the repeat unit rather than length and states limits on count, boundaries and specificity.

Correct metadata and periodic label (bundle-supported). Cites stable 2.08 pinned via release parameter, cites dated periodic identifier in addition when used, rejects citing only 'current'/'latest'. Explains periodic as a dated interim layer on 2.08 carrying newly classified structures, not a new numbered stable release. All must_include met; mention of 'fixes' is a minor hedge, not a material error. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correct a.47.2.1 placement, lineage, protein nodes, fragment comment, 'ms' flag and automated-match comment, all supported. Good interpretation of fragments as reliable for the observed part but not for boundaries, topology or function, with correct fold-vs-superfamily homology semantics and no function transfer. However it describes the full domain as an antiparallel three-helix bundle while also quoting that the three-helical fragments are missing secondary structure, so it never articulates that the full domain's additional helix resolves the spectrin-repeat resemblance; the STAT-like/spectrin-like wording is somewhat conflated.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Covers divergence in c.2.1, convergence possibility, and integrated-evidence requirements, and correctly separates fold from superfamily semantics. However it states that 'different folds make a common origin implausible' and that convergence 'is the likely explanation' for different folds/superfamilies without the caveat that SCOPe separation is a non-assertion rather than evidence against remote homology. c.2.1 lineage verified in bundle; background claims (c.3, SDR/MDR/LDH families) are correct and flagged as unverified.

Correct 2.04 no fold/superfamily link (b.23.2 vs b.18.1) and 2.08 shared superfamily b.18.1 with separate families b.18.1.36 vs b.18.1.3, family 267607. Structure-led remote homology with jelly-roll topology and divergent binding function, chain B split and boundary change noted, firm caveats on no function transfer. Complete.

Lineage, species sunid, comments, and hf definition all supported by the bundle. Homology kept at family/superfamily; hf correctly treated as a structural caveat, not an evolutionary one; rejects template, structure-search, and fold-labelled training use; recommends stratifying by hf, mutation, and ligand state and checking coordinates; states the structural difference was not independently verified. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Meets must_include: homology holds at family level; fr defined and linked to partial correspondence, end gaps, core-only identity/RMSD with coverage reported separately; complete non-fragment domain preferred as representative with quality check, fragments retained as supporting data for protein/species/ligand state. Lengths 104/99 supported by sequence endpoints; lineage, fr annotation and comment supported. Rejects function transfer and separates fold-level similarity from family homology. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.

Concise but complete: correct recommendation; new family claims close ancestry with the superfamily and invites unsafe transfer; new superfamily records topology match without homology, convergence or undetectable divergence left open; new fold only when topology genuinely differs; revisable hypothesis with named evidence types (intermediates, conserved residues, catalytic geometry, genomic context); FATCAT/AlphaFold hits similarity only; no function/template inheritance. No fabricated facts. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct 2.08 placement of the three families under d.144.1 with correct SUNIDs, supported by the bundle. Justifies superfamily-level homology and a shared two-lobe ATP-phosphotransferase core, explicitly denies substrate, regulation and template transfer, and requires same-family/ortholog homology, motif and pocket alignment with pseudokinase checks, biochemistry, complex structures, phylogeny and structure-quality checks (SPACI used correctly as quality, not evolution). Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.
